A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RealDGen work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original SR and LR-generation experiments, extractor and filtering ablations, and a 10-volunteer user study.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds ResShift evaluations, further ablations, additional comparisons, and blurred-image tests.

M1.justification: The extractor pretraining, partial fine-tuning, conditioned diffusion model, losses, and filtering mechanism remain unchanged. Corrected equations and diagrams align with the procedure already described in v3; specifying three filtering candidates adds implementation detail.

E1.justification: The retained RealSR, DRealSR, SmartPhone, and RealVSR coverage expands to blurred REDS images and an internet LR restoration case (A.13 and A.15). A.8 also reports an additional 2x generation setting, although Table 11's identical 2x and 4x scores limit the cross-scale evidence.

E2.justification: Alongside the retained BSRGAN, Real-ESRGAN, and SynDiff comparisons, v4 evaluates bicubic-trained RRDB, RRDB trained on collected RealSR pairs, and a DASR[D] degradation-extractor alternative (Tables 14, 16, and 18). DASR was previously cited but not evaluated in this comparison.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include ResShift fine-tuning for 10,000 iterations after 500,000-iteration pretraining, CLIP-IQA evaluation, real-paired-data training controls, and timing over 100 images. The timing experiment reports 1–30 sampling steps; this does not establish a change to the retained experiments' sampling settings.

E4.justification: v4 adds hyperparameter sweeps, pretraining removal, further fine-tuning analysis, DASR substitution, resource-cost comparisons, real-data augmentation controls, and reference-degradation case studies. Existing filtering, extractor-removal, and RealVSR analyses remain. Tables 9–10 apparently interchange n and margin labels, weakening interpretation of the new sensitivity results.

E5.justification: No new seed counts, repeated-training information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced. The 10-person, 10-image user study and its displayed score distributions remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The original Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results after renumbering. New results include the ResShift fine-tuning comparison (SmartPhone PSNR 27.05 versus 27.27), REDS performance of 23.9834 PSNR and 0.6712 SSIM, and additional ablation, runtime, and parameter measurements. Table 14 reports identical real-only and real-plus-generated results: 27.302 PSNR and 0.7934 SSIM.

T1.justification: Equations 7 and 8 change the content-condition input from x_hr to x_lr, matching LR-only diffusion training already specified in v3's prose and Algorithm 1. This is a local formal-definition correction; the remaining mathematical formulation is retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about unsupervised generation from unpaired LR/HR images, content-degradation decoupling, and improved SR generalization. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: New explanations address LR-to-HR content-feature transfer, avoidance of identity mapping, and differences from DASR's contrastive sampling. A.9–A.10 add speed-quality tradeoffs and explain the advantage of camera-matched real training pairs. However, A.10's claimed augmentation benefit is unsupported by Table 14's identical rows.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies selecting one of three generated candidates, ResShift training budgets, and timing hardware, sample count, and inclusion of I/O. Existing architecture and training details largely remain. The explicit BasicSR URL is removed, although the framework remains named.

R1.justification: v4 adds contrastive-learning, ResShift, REDS, and recent generative/restoration references, while removing some earlier citations, including Fritsche and Zhou. A.14 explains the distinction from already-cited DASR. The central positioning against manual collection, physical degradation models, and learned generators remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely intact, with localized rewrites and expanded explanations. v4 updates the author/header text, adopts author-year citations, moves references before the appendix, and subdivides the extractor discussion. The retained scientific sections are not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 2 and 9–18 and Figures 5, 10, and 13. Figures 1–2 are redrawn, including corrected contrastive-sample labels and an explicit HR content branch. Conference formatting and figure placement change substantially; existing user-study and DRealSR panels are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: Corrected conditioning equations and Figure 2 resolve inconsistencies in v3, while new extractor comparisons, ResShift evaluation, and blurred-input tests strengthen validation. The gain is limited by new reporting problems: apparently swapped hyperparameter labels, duplicated cross-scale scores, and an augmentation claim unsupported by Table 14. These tradeoffs support a limited overall improvement.
